phase: STEP B (manifest + regression tests). STEP A (diagnostic shutdown) deliberately NOT done: ruled unsafe as drafted; B goes first.
description: Declarative inventory of the security plane. Every control names its hook, its registration (event + matchers), the files it sources, the properties that make it trustworthy, and a fixture that demonstrates it firing. A control absent from this manifest is not protected by the regression tests; a control present here cannot be unregistered or deleted silently. The gaps array names what #45 demands and does not exist yet — a manifest that lists only what exists would fake coverage.
invariants: Fail-closed on every path: permission-guard v2.1.0 (#58), repo-boundary _emit_deny_on_crash trap, k8s gate blocks kubectl without an explicit --context
Delegate contracts verified in source before enforcement (T16): git-safety-guard.py emits JSON on every terminal path (deny = JSON + exit 1; the JSON is authoritative)
Direct registration of repo-boundary-guard.sh on Edit|Write and Agent|Task in addition to Bash: the boundary does not depend on a single wrapper

properties: v2.1.0, hardened in #58 (T16+T19): fail-closed on every path — delegate missing/crashed/empty/unparseable denies; unparseable stdin denies; premature death denies via idempotent ERR/EXIT trap (a naive trap double-echoes the deny under set -e, producing unparseable output = a bypass; the flag prevents it)
Dispatches to both guards below; a real deny arriving as JSON + exit 1 is propagated intact (JSON is authoritative, not the exit code)
Delegate stderr preserved: logged to ~/.ralph/permission-guard.log and re-emitted
Blocks destructive git (reset --hard, push --force), destructive fs (rm -rf /, clean -f) and command chaining (;, &&, eval, xargs rm)
Stdlib-only python (json/os/re/shlex/subprocess/sys) — no repo files sourced, no hidden dependencies
Contract (verified T16): allow/ask print JSON + exit 0, deny prints JSON + exit 1 — JSON on every terminal path (CRIT-002 allow_and_exit)
Registered DIRECTLY on Edit|Write and Agent|Task (inserted before the permission pipeline) in addition to Bash — the boundary survives a broken wrapper
Own fail-closed trap _emit_deny_on_crash on ERR/EXIT (lines 15-18): a crash denies, logged to ~/.ralph/logs/repo-boundary.log

Its source of lib/worktree-utils.sh (line 36) carries a '|| { inline fallback implementations }' that is NOT fail-open: it defines in-repo replacements for get_project_root/get_main_repo and the script still fails closed — it degrades with dignity

Boundary semantics: the guard denies paths inside OTHER git repos under GITHUB_DIR (~/Documents/GitHub, line 25) and allows everything else BY DESIGN (is_allowed_path tail: 'Allow other paths (system, etc.)') — it is a GitHub-repo boundary, not a filesystem boundary. A path outside GITHUB_DIR is never denied, no matter what it is; fixtures must target another repo under GITHUB_DIR (the fixture isolates it by overriding HOME for the guard invocation)

KNOWN DEFECT (found by this baseline's fixture work, 2026-08-25, fix out of T20 scope): canonicalize() failure emits the sentinel __CANONICALIZE_FAILED__ which is NEVER checked downstream — the log says 'denying as precaution' but the sentinel flows into 'Allow other paths' and the verdict is ALLOW. Repro: Edit/Write to a nonexistent out-of-repo path with a nonexistent parent dir (e.g. an invented nested path). Additionally the second fallback 'realpath -m' is a no-op on macOS ('illegal option -- m', verified rc=1), so on stock macOS canonicalize relies solely on the dir+base chain. Adjacent asymmetry: GITHUB_DIR (line 25) is built from raw $HOME without canonicalization while paths ARE canonicalized — through a symlinked HOME/Documents the other-repo branch can silently fail to match (observed with symlinked /tmp and /var on macOS)

fixture.run: d="$(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && pwd -P)" && mkdir -p "$d/Documents/GitHub/fr" && git -C "$d/Documents/GitHub/fr" init -q && printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/Documents/GitHub/fr/x.md"}}' "$d" | HOME="$d" bash .claude/hooks/repo-boundary-guard.sh; rc=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $rc

properties: Context-aware: every kubectl/helm/minikube command must declare --context explicitly (kubectl_context_required otherwise); --context must be a static name (kubectl_context_not_static)
Factual minikube verification rather than name-matching; kubectl verbs delegated from git-safety by design (handoff)
Known over-reach, cataloged (QTEAM_FAILURE_MODES #22): can block unrelated commands that merely reference hook scripts — visible, not silent
Provides get_project_root / get_main_repo (worktree-aware, via --git-common-dir) to the boundary guard and the worktree guards
Not registered itself: consumed via source. repo-boundary-guard.sh carries inline fallbacks if this lib is unreachable (see repo-boundary properties)

gaps.description: #45 demands preventing secrets from entering ordinary (non-audit) work. audit-secrets.js only LOGS 20+ secret patterns post-execution (PostToolUse detection); nothing blocks or warns at write time. Detection-after-the-fact is not the demanded control.
No control screens for RED/toxic content in what the agent produces or relays. Nothing exists to register.
No control governs MCP egress (which servers may be called with what payload). MCP tool calls bypass the Bash/Edit permission surface entirely.
brew/pip/npm installs are governed by a RULE (global CLAUDE.md approval requirement) but by no hook — rules constrain the model, not the tool call. git-safety does not cover package managers.

repo-boundary-guard.sh checks paths, but symlink-following escapes (an in-repo symlink pointing outside) are only partially covered. Declared partial until a fixture proves symlink resolution is boundary-checked.
